title: How Does Wi-Fi Work?
description: Wi-Fi is your home’s own little radio station. Kip and Bub explain what the router does, why walls and distance make it weaker, and simple ways to get a better signal.

scenes.say: Your Wi-Fi works great in the living room, but in the bedroom it crawls. Why?
Today on Tech from Scratch: how does Wi-Fi work?
Wi-Fi is a way to connect your devices without wires, using radio waves. The same basic idea as a radio station, just much shorter range.

card.text: Wi-Fi uses radio waves instead of wires.
card.sub: Like a tiny radio station in your home

scenes.say: The heart of it is your router. The internet comes into your home on a cable. The router takes that connection and broadcasts it through the air to your phone, laptop, and TV.

Here's a common mix-up. Wi-Fi is not the internet. Wi-Fi is just the link between your device and your router. If the router's own connection goes down, you can have full Wi-Fi bars and still no internet.
So why is the bedroom slow? Radio waves get weaker with distance, and things in the way soak them up. Thick walls, floors, metal, even a big aquarium.

A few easy fixes. Put the router up high, out in the open, near the middle of your home, not in a cabinet. Restart it if things get sluggish. And for big homes, a mesh system adds extra stations around the house.
And one more: give it a password. A locked network keeps strangers off your Wi-Fi.

card.text: Always lock your Wi-Fi with a password.
